verdicts.note: Checked against the Legislature roll-call service (S5, S10-S13; S5 re-fetched live 2026-10-08): nay on ESSB 6346 Senate final passage (2026-02-16) and on concurrence/final passage (2026-03-11); nay on Senate passage and final passage of ESSB 5801, ESSB 5813 and ESSB 5814, and on ESHB 2081 final passage. The pamphlet (S1) and issues page (S3) add explicit statements (voted against a gas tax increase and small-business taxes, proposed a sales tax cut, 'NO on tax increases'). These are many independent sources beyond the lone ESSB 6346 vote, so -2/high satisfies the addendum rule.
Rests on S1 and S16, both re-verified; S18 is carried from the primary but not needed for the score.
High is supported: abortion protections and SB 5777 sponsorship on the issues page, the home-page action list, and the Planned Parenthood endorsement in the pamphlet.

S6 confirms yea on ESHB 1296 Senate final passage (2025-04-11). Her only other ESHB 1296 roll call was a nay on Gildon amendment 370, which removed the penalty withholding basic-education funds from noncompliant districts. That concerns enforcement against districts, not parental notification or opt-outs, so it does not cut the other way. +1/medium is the right magnitude for a single final-passage vote.

The evidence is the pamphlet line about 'saying no to outside special interests' and a donation-page line saying there are 'No consultants taking 30 points off the top'. Neither is a structural-reform position (PAC refusal, term limits, dark-money limits, RCV); both are generic campaign framing. Keep the direction but lower confidence to low.
